title: Voyage Static World Rubric v1.6 — Universal Anchor + Adaptive Genre Paths
claim: 100% source-only static design rubric with precommitted specialist weight paths. Predictive validity is not established; no gameplay, narrator generations, published metrics, reader panels or competitor dashboards are required.

grades.3: substantially specified with concrete field links and minor gaps
grades.4: coherently and comprehensively specified, source-traceable, internally consistent
grades.NE: required source evidence missing; no playtest request
grades.NA: genuinely inapplicable with denominator adjustment only where explicitly permitted

grading.formula: Universal uses original v1.5 criterion weights; specialist uses preregistered path weights, optional entry overlay, shared 0..4 static grades. Round final total only, to nearest 0.25.
grading.unknown_policy: NE = necessary artifact missing or feature owner/contract undisclosed; NEVER require playtesting. Do not award 4 for a mere assertion. Mark uncertain engine features unverified.

overrides.NE: report interval and evidence gap; never normalize missing weights away

evidence_strength_caps.missing_feature_owner: For claimed signature mechanics, D1 grade <= 1 unless explicit host, engine, mod or model-guided specification with input/output and limits exists.
evidence_strength_caps.persistence_without_owner: D2 grade <= 1 if advertised durability lacks authoritative data/contract owner; check G4/G11 truthfulness.
evidence_strength_caps.unactionable_opening: A1 grade <= 2 if no named immediately usable affordance is authored.
evidence_strength_caps.creator_conflict: K-C <= 50% if unresolved compatible field precedence; fail G13 for critical false status/authority.

sections.description: Acquisition potential: does the listing generate a desirable and accurate expectation?
First-use activation: does the opening fulfill the promise quickly and without friction?
Engagement potential: does the world generate rewarding decisions over time?
Execution: do the systems and continuity reliably honor what was promised?

criteria.name: Desirable, specific player fantasy
criteria.full_credit: The player can name who they are, what makes that life interesting, and why they want to experience it in one sentence.
criteria.test: S03: identify specific player position, desired action and compelling constraint in the listing and authored start.
criteria.tradeoff: A specific promise attracts curiosity; overly narrow identity may reduce audience, but a generic "do anything" promise puts all imagination work on the player.

criteria.name: Distinctive but comprehensible hook
criteria.full_credit: A recognizable genre template plus one memorable differentiation; unusual bodies, social roles, special powers, predicaments, or concrete local culture all qualify.
criteria.test: S03/S10: identify distinctive action/identity compared with static genre-neighbor listings.
criteria.tradeoff: Extreme novelty can narrow appeal or raise onboarding costs; pure familiarity can become forgettable. No bonus for novelty without action consequences.

criteria.name: Cover and title deliver the fantasy
criteria.full_credit: Cover scores up to 6 points from the 100-point Cover Diagnostic; public listing title scores up to 2 points from its independent 100-point Title Diagnostic. Paired card communicates the accurate player fantasy.
criteria.test: S10: offline cover crop, thumbnail hierarchy, title fit and C-A…C-J/T-A…T-H grading; source truth check.
criteria.tradeoff: Do not optimize for polish, keyword density, or hype over genuine click-relevant expectation. Complementary evocative/informative title–cover pairs are valid; deception is not.

criteria.name: Discover-page blurb converts promise into playable expectations
criteria.full_credit: Blurb /100 diagnostic demonstrates playable role, distinctive first action and loop; major claims verified; meaningful choices and audience fit clear.
criteria.test: S11: excerpt at 160/300/600 characters; trace top three advertised features to source owners.
criteria.tradeoff: Short hooks convert attention into interest; longer descriptions may add depth but must not bury the first action or substitute feature counts for play. Grade via blurb diagnostic only, not a separate 0–4 grade.

criteria.name: Concrete opening with a real decision
criteria.full_credit: The default start establishes place, situation, relevant constraints and one or more meaningful next actions without scripting the player’s response.
criteria.test: S04: enumerate immediate written affordances in every start without generating narration.
criteria.tradeoff: A directed opening aids activation; an intrusive opening that chooses feelings, speech or a quest for the player undermines agency.

criteria.name: Signature fantasy pays off promptly
criteria.full_credit: The authored opening or immediate source-defined transition makes the signature role/power/activity tangible and specifies a plausible consequence; actual timing unknown.
criteria.test: S04: trace visible signature experience from authored first scene/defined immediate situation and consequence.
criteria.tradeoff: Too-early total power can trivialize play; too much setup can make the world feel like false advertising. Payoff can be discovery or bond, not only power.

criteria.name: Player has a concrete place in the world
criteria.full_credit: A believable initial relationship, responsibility, opportunity, resource need, geographical situation, institutional membership, or rival ecology creates context without compulsory destiny.
criteria.test: S04: identify existing belonging, need, relationship or place independent of a forced main quest.
criteria.tradeoff: Social anchoring is helpful in social worlds; solitary monster/ship settings can use physical needs and responsibilities instead. Do not demand a romance interest.

criteria.name: Creation and onboarding are low-friction
criteria.full_credit: Authored/default entry path, question burden and optional depth are clear in source; undocumented platform UI behavior remains NE.
criteria.test: S05/S06: review authored mandatory fields, defaults, quickstart contract and word burden; do not time a UI.
criteria.tradeoff: Deep custom creation is a bonus only when skippable or staged. Making new players read every faction, stat and species first imposes a cost.

criteria.name: Repeatable, genre-specific core loop
criteria.full_credit: A fully documented repeatable action → condition → effect → new opportunity loop exists, with at least one coherent variation where appropriate.
criteria.test: S07: construct source-backed loop graph activity → condition → effect → altered affordance; no turns.
criteria.tradeoff: A genre-specific loop is more valuable than dozens of labeled game modes that change only difficulty or tone.

criteria.name: Compounding and legible progression
criteria.full_credit: Progression rules define changed options, prerequisites and authorized effects; no test sessions are implied.
criteria.test: S07: map progression prerequisites and at least three source-defined transitions.
criteria.tradeoff: Not every world needs levels or upward power; social/knowledge/moral progression counts. Unbounded escalation may erase meaningful decisions.

criteria.name: Real player agency and viable variation
criteria.full_credit: The player can pursue, decline, pause, switch or fail the central path; alternate goals operate within coherent rules instead of reverting to the author’s expected plot.
criteria.test: S09: inspect authored refusal, delay, decline, alternate-activity and failure outcomes.
criteria.tradeoff: Freedom without constraints is directionless; constraints without credible alternatives feel railroaded. Genre-respecting variation matters more than every world supporting everything.

criteria.name: Responsive cast OR active environment
criteria.full_credit: NPC goals/schedules/knowledge boundaries or equivalent environment/faction dynamics are concretely specified.
criteria.test: S08/S12: trace NPC/ecology active-state goals, schedules, bounded knowledge and source contradictions.
criteria.tradeoff: Do not reward NPC count by itself. A smaller recurring cast can be more useful than hundreds of silent entries; high-quality isolation is valid when deliberate.

criteria.name: Enjoyable downtime, pacing and tonal consistency
criteria.full_credit: The game allows recovery, work, friendship, routine, craft, solitude and aftermath without forced threats; its typical dialogue and consequences consistently feel like the promised genre.
criteria.test: S09/S12: inspect authored downtime activities and guidance against forced tone/romance/hazard.
criteria.tradeoff: Constant escalation can exhaust players; excessive low-stakes wandering can become empty if there is no compelling latent loop.

criteria.name: Signature mechanics: source contract traceability
criteria.full_credit: Top three advertised mechanics have explicit owner, inputs, relevant state/condition, outputs, limits and promises aligned with source; runtime efficacy not asserted.
criteria.test: S03: source trace of three strongest feature promises to owners, inputs, outputs and limits; no execution claims.
criteria.tradeoff: Do not equate zero native triggers with failure: mods or generation may own behavior. Also do not equate long instructions with reliable execution.

criteria.name: Continuity and consequence integrity
criteria.full_credit: Authoritative state identities, reads/writes/merges/one-shot guards or documented external continuity contracts support advertised durability without contradictory ownership.
criteria.test: S08: inspect authoritative continuity fields/contracts, one-shot guards and reconciliation.
criteria.tradeoff: Overtracking every minor event wastes context; retain consequential facts and compress noise. LC can own reusable continuity as a separate mod.

criteria.name: Believable world, calibrated friction and voice
criteria.full_credit: World logic and narrator contracts are consistent across starts, locations, abilities, economies, ecology and permitted unusual goals.
criteria.test: S12: static consistency review of society, material needs, travel, risk, narration and NPC knowledge.
criteria.tradeoff: Tight world focus can beat broad maps. Genre-specific danger is fine; arbitrary punishments and mechanical contradictions break the promise.

gates.name: Engine/schema safety
gates.description: Offline JSON/schema parse with fields, types, IDs, references and conditions; schema coverage marked NE if unavailable.

gates.name: Player agency
gates.description: Authored starts and narrator guidance never prescribe unchosen PC speech, assent, romantic intent, emotions or unauthorized status.

gates.name: Signature promise integrity
gates.description: Top three claims link to declared source owner, starting affordance, input/output contract and limits, or are explicitly labeled as narrative intent.

gates.name: Continuity and causal memory
gates.description: Source states authoritative identity/state, update, merge and restoration ownership; no critical contradiction of advertised persistence.

gates.name: Viable scope/alternatives
gates.description: Authored choice/refusal or disclosed linear scope agrees with listing.

gates.name: Honest listing and audience fit
gates.description: Title, cover, blurb, ratings, IP claims, tags and mechanics accurately reflect source.

gates.name: Mechanics agreement
gates.description: Stats, economy, combat, permissions, biology and other state systems are internally coherent.

gates.name: External mod ownership
gates.description: Declared external module dependency/version/contract is traceable and no duplicate conflicting owner; mandatory absent evidence prevents verified readiness.

gates.name: Cover integrity / visual promise
gates.description: Offline visual crop/reduction, C-A..C-J floors, accurate depicted genre/role; no human panel.

gates.name: Listing title integrity
gates.description: Correct title, no placeholders, dishonest IP or feature claims; offline title truncation/card match and source premise check.

gates.name: Discover blurb integrity and first-action comprehension
gates.description: Opening 160/300/600-character excerpts, source-backed key promises, readable layout and truth against cover/title/starts; no reader survey.

gates.name: Start coherence and playable agency
gates.description: All offered authored starts define available action/handoff/status, respect creator compatibility and consent, and match genre.
gates.fail_response: BLOCK broken start/critical contradiction; otherwise REVIEW weak first scene

gates.name: Creator truth and compatibility
gates.description: Authored questions/options/defaults are distinct and factual, with role/start/mode precedence and legitimate effect ownership.
gates.fail_response: BLOCK critical contradiction or false mandatory choice; otherwise REVISE wording/source wording

story_start_rubric.name: Voyage Story-Start Static Design Diagnostic

rubric.name: Playable scene / situation
rubric.full_credit: Concrete first-scene prose OR narrator instruction specifying place, actors, accessible props and handoff; no generated scene required.

rubric.name: Character position and constraints
rubric.full_credit: Player knows where they are, their relevant role, what is already true, and which important things are NOT already granted.

rubric.name: Actionable affordances
rubric.full_credit: At least one meaningful next action exists now; people/objects/routes/questions can be engaged without asking the narrator to invent the premise.

rubric.name: First-scene signature payoff
rubric.full_credit: Opening visibly delivers a distinctive aspect of the promised fantasy; payoffs can be social, contemplative, comedic, exploratory, survival-related, or mechanical.

rubric.name: Tone, pacing and ordinary-life validity
rubric.full_credit: Experience matches advertised tone; neither forced threat nor forced tranquility is imposed against the intended genre.

rubric.name: Distinctness of each authored start
rubric.full_credit: Alternative starts change initial situation, role, stakes, resources, or social position—not just names or scenery.

rubric.name: Agency, consent and optionality
rubric.full_credit: No fabricated player dialogue, feelings, decisions, coercive jobs, romance or irreversible authority. NPCs/environment can act independently.

rubric.name: Character-creator compatibility
rubric.full_credit: Start honors selected species, status, history, abilities, goals and mode; conflicts have explicit precedence or are flagged/resolved.

rubric.name: Scene determinacy and instruction hygiene
rubric.full_credit: Explicit source facts, actor behaviors, action affordances, precedence and handoff; reusable guidance not duplicated. Runtime consistency not assumed.

character_creator_rubric.name: Voyage Character-Creation Static Clarity Diagnostic

rubric.name: Player-facing question clarity
rubric.full_credit: Each prompt tells the player what they are deciding in natural second-person language; avoid boilerplate about how the engine respects choices.

rubric.name: Distinct choices and consequences
rubric.full_credit: Each option gives specific starting knowledge, affordance, skill, contact, constraint, tone or recurring opportunity; mechanics are not required for every option.

rubric.name: Internal coherence and precedence
rubric.full_credit: Story start, role, species, background, mode and goal cannot silently contradict or override one another; precedence and compatibility are explicit.

rubric.name: Low-friction path to first action
rubric.full_credit: Source specifies sensible defaults/skipping/quickstart and avoids unnecessary mandatory lore decisions; no timed taps required.

rubric.name: Signature-fantasy relevance
rubric.full_credit: Core decisions shape what the player gets to do or be in the promised world rather than collecting generic biography trivia.

rubric.name: Scope, agency and reversibility
rubric.full_credit: Distinguish fixed starting facts from aspirations and tone preferences; allow goals to evolve; do not assign mental states.

rubric.name: Readable options and accessible UI
rubric.full_credit: Labels and option text are concise, distinguishable and plausibly fit mobile text layouts; static proxy only.

rubric.name: Fast-entry alternatives
rubric.full_credit: Quickstart/default/premade/example character when appropriate; no requirement for premades if a simple creator already provides fast entry.

selection.precommit: Select path and optional entry overlay BEFORE assigning any grades or examining popularity results for this candidate. Record immutable path-selection rationale and artifact hash.
signal_sources: Source-backed repeatable loop or progression contract
selection.rule: Choose the single specialist path if at least two of the three source signals support it. Otherwise use universal or documented hybrid. Path choice must not be based on which score is higher.
selection.hybrid: If two paths are genuinely co-primary, preregister primary + secondary BEFORE scoring, and blend their criterion weights at 0.70/0.30. No more than two paths. Universal anchor always retained.
selection.overlay_rule: Entry overlay is optional; select exactly one of standard, creator_first, fixed_identity from source evidence, never from score optimization. Apply delta to each path/blend before scoring; section totals unchanged.
selection.edition_policy: Mods, patches, engines and frameworks are not standalone playable worlds; route them to a mod-system quality assessment. Do not force a world score on a mod listing.
selection.ip_policy: Original, licensed and fan-inspired IP are reported as audience/attribution/confound metadata; award no automatic points for established fandom; enforce truthful IP/public package framing and accessible source-specific context.
selection.maturity_policy: Concept, design draft, full exported world have different evidence coverage. All are statically inspectable; incomplete stage is scored as an interval and never certified release ready.

universal.name: Universal / Open-ended Sandbox
universal.trigger: No single primary loop is demonstrably dominant, or use as cross-genre comparison anchor.
static_probes: Two meaningfully different documented repeatable activities
Both a default and at least one alternative player approach are coherent
World breadth does not substitute for traceable consequences
universal.note: Always calculate this score, even when another specialist path is selected.

progression.name: Progression / Power Growth
progression.trigger: Primary repeatable reward is acquiring, transforming, combining or advancing powers, status or capabilities.
static_probes: At least three concrete source-defined progression transitions with prerequisites
Costs, bounds and failure/alternative paths stated where material
First authored scene exposes meaningful agency around the signature capability
progression.note: L2 and A2 gain weight; pure complexity and giant ability lists do not.

social.name: Social / Relationship Sandbox
social.trigger: Primary repeated activity is interaction, relationship building, conflict, reputation or social negotiation.
static_probes: At least two differentiated independent NPC goals or social situations
Written knowledge boundaries and consequence updates for key relationships
Actionable social setting exists without mandatory romance or forced protagonist speech
social.note: L3/L4 gain weight; number of NPCs and romance availability are not proxies.

survival.name: Survival / Environmental Exploration
survival.trigger: Primary repeatable activity is navigating material constraints, threats, ecology, transport or exploration.
static_probes: Source-backed danger/resource/route feedback and recovery
At least two distinct actions with different survival consequences
Consistent body, equipment, hazard and resource limits
survival.note: A1 and L1 gain weight; survival worlds need not force combat.

management.name: Management / Craft / Institution
management.trigger: Primary repeatable activity is operating systems, businesses, organizations, workshops or settlements.
static_probes: At least one resource-input → work → output → trade-off loop
Decisions alter feasible subsequent operations and NPC/institution state
Player role, contractual authority and refusal paths are consistent
management.note: L1/L2 and D1 gain weight; a detailed economy table alone does not score well.

mystery.name: Mystery / Investigation
mystery.trigger: Primary repeated activity is obtaining, interpreting, testing and acting on information.
static_probes: Clue-and-inference graph with multiple independent evidence routes
No essential solution depends on an unprompted narrator invention
False leads, privacy/knowledge limits and resolution alternatives stated
mystery.note: A1/A3 and D2 gain importance; not every secret needs to be exposed at the start.

cozy_life.name: Cozy / Life Simulation
cozy_life.trigger: Primary repeatable activity is everyday relationships, work, care, routines, exploration or self-directed life.
static_probes: At least two sustainable low-stakes agency loops
Ordinary choices have concrete social/material consequences without forced crises
Routines, time and NPC autonomy are specified consistently
cozy_life.note: L3/L4/L5 gain weight; absence of urgency is not a defect.

identity_transformation.name: Identity / Transformation / Rebirth
identity_transformation.trigger: Primary appeal is becoming or inhabiting a distinct identity, creature, role, unusual embodiment or life change.
static_probes: Form/status/power choice has distinct source-backed situational implications
First situation respects the selected identity without unearned authority
Creator options are coherent with starts, biology, status and actual limits
identity_transformation.note: P1 and A4 gain weight; species count and creator size earn no automatic points.

creator_first.name: Creator-first entry
creator_first.trigger: Role-defining choices are explicitly part of the advertised primary fantasy, and source-backed creator semantics are supplied.

fixed_identity.name: Fixed identity / immediate scene
fixed_identity.trigger: The offered default character is strongly authored or explicitly premade with meaningful immediately available actions; creator depth is not a promised differentiator.

scoring.scale: Criterion grades from 0 through 4 based solely on verifiable static artifacts. The original v1.5 category diagnostics and caps continue to apply.
scoring.general_formula: For 0..4 integer-graded ordinary criteria: w_i * g_i/4. UNIVERSAL baseline retains v1.5 per-criterion quarter rounding (including adjusted P3/P4); specialist/adaptive uses unrounded contributions, rounds only final total to nearest 0.25. Never round weight matrices before grading.
scoring.score_comparability: Rank different genres on universal /100 only. Within the same preregistered specialist path, adaptive /100 can guide trade-offs. Never choose the larger of universal/adaptive as a winner score.
scoring.missing_data: For each NE criterion, lower bound assumes zero and upper bound assumes four. For partially missing presentation diagnostics, keep that entire criterion NE. Never rescale observed points to 100. Label missing art/source honestly.
scoring.release_standard: Only a fully evidenced 100-point score, all applicable gates PASS, universal >=85, specialist >=85, and section floors reached can earn STATIC READY; this is not a runtime certification or probability.
scoring.uncertainty: Report evidence completeness (weighted fraction of fully scored criteria), 0..100 score interval, missing static artifacts, source/version discrepancies, and all gate statuses.
scoring.hypothesis_policy: Historical public actions/bookmarks, last-update dates, observed creator dashboards, and rollout age MUST NOT enter candidate scoring. Retrospective analytics are strictly separate exploratory evidence.
scoring.universal_rounding: Preserve v1.5 exact score convention: each individual criterion contribution rounded to nearest 0.25, then summed.
scoring.specialist_rounding: Compute contributions at full precision then round final score to nearest 0.25.

output_contract: universal and selected specialist score or intervals

story_start.name: Promise-to-entry trace
story_start.requirement: Map the main listing promise to the default authored situation, an immediately available action and its source-defined consequence.

story_start.name: Entry-path coverage
story_start.requirement: For every offered start, verify selected role/form/status is not silently contradicted, even if the start is shorter or deliberately open-ended.

story_start.name: Affordance diversity, not quantity
story_start.requirement: Confirm meaningful alternatives that differ in objective or consequence; do not reward choice menus purely by count.

story_start.name: Format neutrality
story_start.requirement: Prose and instructional starts may both qualify if first situation, interactable elements, handoff, rules and source consequences are explicit.

character_creator.name: Choice value vs verbosity
character_creator.requirement: Flag options whose text differs only by substituted label, unless clearly marked cosmetic.

character_creator.name: Progressive disclosure
character_creator.requirement: Inspect documented default/quickstart or simple path, then optional advanced depth; no tap-time claims.

character_creator.name: Player-status consistency
character_creator.requirement: Map factual status, aspirational goal, preexisting relationships and starting authority across every creator/start/mode conflict class.

character_creator.name: Identity fantasy bridge
character_creator.requirement: Trace creator-defining choices to authored first-situation affordances and later source-defined world responses.

optional_new_hard_checks.name: Path and scoring provenance
optional_new_hard_checks.test: World type, primary genre and optional overlay preregistered before grades; source version/hash documented. If unknown, universal only; never optimize path for score.
optional_new_hard_checks.effect: Blocks specialized certification when omitted; not an extra weighted criterion.

optional_new_hard_checks.name: Claim-to-start/creator alignment
optional_new_hard_checks.test: Static trace of the first-screen listing promise to a start affordance, meaningful creator option/default and governed follow-on activity; document intentional exceptions.
optional_new_hard_checks.effect: Blocks material contradictions; not a requirement for custom creator categories.

readiness_v1_6_superseding.note: Do not confuse design readiness with demonstrated success. Old v1.5 fixed section floors apply to universal anchor; v1.6 derived floors apply to adaptive paths.
